A piece (of food, metal, wood etc.) having this shape.
To support or secure using a wedge.
To force into a narrow gap.

wedge.ety: From Middle English wegge (“wedge”), from Old English weċġ (“wedge”), from Proto-West Germanic *wagi, from Proto-Germanic *wagjaz.

ex.ja: パイをもう一ついかがですか。

yuri.ety: Borrowed from Japanese 百合(ゆり) (yuri, “lily”), by analogy to 薔薇(バラ) (bara, “rose”), indicating love. See Yuri (genre) § “Terminology and etymology” at Wikipedia.

ex.ja: 百合は当時たびたびロンドンに行った。

en: Causing or tending to cause addiction; habit-forming.
Enjoyable, so that one comes back for more.
A drug that causes an addiction.
Anything that is very habit-forming.

ex.en: Is nicotine as addictive as heroin?
ex.ja: ニコチンはヘロインと同様に中毒性があるのですか？

en: A natural attraction or feeling of kinship to a person or thing.
A family relationship through marriage of a relative (e.g. sister-in-law), as opposed to consanguinity (e.g. sister).

affinity.ety: From Middle English affinite, from Old French affinité. Ostensibly equivalent to affine + -ity. See also af-.

ex.en: This case has an affinity with that one.
ex.ja: この事件はあの事件と似たところがある。

ex.en: They feel a strange affinity with each other.
ex.ja: 彼らは妙におたがいに気が合う。

ex.en: I feel a strong affinity for her.
ex.ja: 彼女がとても好きです。

en: A metal that is a combination of two or more elements, at least one of which is a metal, a base metal.
An admixture; something added which stains, taints etc.
To mix or combine; often used of metals.
To reduce the purity of by mixing with a less valuable substance.

alloy.ety: Borrowed from Middle French alloy, aloy, from Old French aloi, from aloiier, from Latin alligō.

ex.en: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.
ex.ja: 真鍮は銅と亜鉛の合金である。

ex.en: Bronze-ware is largely made from alloys of brass and tin.
ex.ja: 青銅器は主として銅と錫の合金で出来ている。

ex.ja: ＯＤＳスーパーアロイは粉末冶金技術を伴うメカニカルアロイ法により製造されます。

en: The policy of racial segregation in South Africa from 1948 to 1994.
Any similar policy of racial segregation or separation and discrimination, particularly when in favor of a minority rule.
To impose a policy of segregation of groups of people, especially one based on race.

English apartheid
Borrowed from Afrikaans apartheid (literally “separateness, apartness”) (1929 in a South African socio-political context), from Afrikaans apart (“separate”) + suffix -heid, cognate of English -hood.

en: Inflammation of a joint or joints causing pain and/or disability, swelling and stiffness, and due to various causes such as infection, tr…

arthritis.ety: From Latin arthrītis, from Ancient Greek ἀρθρῖτις (arthrîtis, “joint-disease, gout”), from ἄρθρον (árthron, “a joint”). By surface analysis, arthr- + -itis.

en: Evil, especially considered as an active force for destruction or death.
Suffering, woe, torment.
To wrap into a bale.

bale.ety:
From Middle English bale (“evil”), from Old English bealu, from Proto-West Germanic *balu, from Proto-Germanic *balwą.
Cognate with Low German bal- (“bad, ill”), Gothic 𐌱𐌰𐌻𐍅𐌴𐌹𐌽𐍃 (balweins, “torture”), Old High German balo (“destruction”), Old Norse bǫl (“disaster”).

en: A semiaquatic rodent of the genus Castor, having a wide, flat tail and webbed feet, native to the Northern Hemisphere.
The fur of the beaver.
To form a felt-like texture, similar to the way beaver fur is used for felt-making.
To work hard.

beaver.ety:
From Middle English bever, from Old English befer, from Proto-West Germanic *bebru, from Proto-Germanic *bebruz, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰébʰrus (“beaver”).
Cognate with West Frisian bever, Dutch bever, French bièvre, German Biber, dialectal Swedish bjur. Non-Germanic cognates include Welsh befer, Latin fiber, Lithuanian bẽbras, Russian бобр (bobr), Avestan 𐬠𐬀𐬎𐬎𐬭𐬀 (bauura), and Sanskrit बभ्रु (bábhru, “mongoose; ichneumon”).
Slang use to refer to a woman evolved from use to refer to pubic hair, which evolved from use to refer to beards, which evolved from use to refer to the furry animal or

ex.en: I've been beavering away studying for entrance exams.
ex.ja: バリバリの受験生です。

ex.en: Beavers rarely inflict damage on people.
ex.ja: ビーバーは人に危害を加えることはめったにない。

ex.en: He is an eager beaver.
ex.ja: 彼は仕事の鬼だ。

en: A brag; ostentatious positive appraisal of oneself.
Something that one brags about.
To brag; to talk loudly in praise of oneself.
[with about or of] To speak of with pride, vanity, or exultation, with a view to self-commendation; to extol.

boast.ety:
From Middle English bosten, from bost (“boast, glory, noise, arrogance, presumption, pride, vanity”), probably of North Germanic origin, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *bausuz (“inflated, swollen, puffed up, proud, arrogant, bad”).
Cognate with Scots bost, boist (“to threaten, brag, boast”), Anglo-Norman bost (“ostentation”) (from Germanic). Related to Norwegian baus (“proud, bold, daring”), dialectal German baustern (“to swell”), German böse (“evil, bad, angry”), Dutch boos (“evil, wicked, angry”), West Frisian boas (“bad, wicked, angry, shrewd, clever”). Compare also dialectal Norwegian baus

ex.en: If not a lie, close to a boast.
ex.ja: 嘘ではないにしろ、ホラに近い。

ex.en: He boasted of having won the first prize.
ex.ja: 彼は１等をとった事を自慢した。

ex.en: I am sick to death of his boasts.
ex.ja: 彼の自慢話はまったく聞き飽きた。

en: The person who makes a telephone call.
A visitor.

caller.ety: From Middle English callar, equivalent to call + -er.

ex.en: The caller refused to give us his name.
ex.ja: 電話をかけた者は名前を教えるのを拒否した。

ex.en: The caller hung up without saying anything.
ex.ja: 相手は何も言わずに電話を切ったんだ。

ex.en: Tom always checks the caller ID before he answers the phone.
ex.ja: トムは電話に出る前にいつも発信元の電話番号を確認している。

en: A hollow area within the body.
The female part of a mold: the depression itself or (metonymically) the half of the mold that contains it.

cavity.ety: From Middle French cavité or Late Latin cavitās, from cav(i) (“hollow, excavated, concave”) + -tās (“-ity”, nominal suffix). First attested in the Mid-16th c.

ex.en: I have a lot of cavities now.
ex.ja: 今は虫歯だらけだ。

ex.en: I think I have a cavity.
ex.ja: どうも虫歯のようです。

ex.en: If we care for our teeth we won't have cavities.
ex.ja: 歯をきちんと手入れしていれば虫歯にはならない。

en: A man, a fellow.
A child.
Of the skin, to split or flake due to cold weather or dryness.
To cause to open in slits or chinks; to split; to cause the skin of to crack or become rough.

chap.ety: Clipping of chapman (“dealer, customer”) in 16th-century English.

ex.en: In the winter, my lips would chap.
ex.ja: 冬になると唇が割れたりする。

ex.en: Our lips get chapped in winter.
ex.ja: 冬になると唇が割れたりする。

ex.ja: 毎年冬になると唇がカサカサに乾燥してしまいます。

en: A young male horse or similar young male equine, especially just after birth or less than a year old.
A young crane (bird).
To frisk or frolic like a colt; to act licentiously or wantonly.

colt.ety: From Middle English colt, from Old English colt, from Proto-Germanic *kultaz (“plump; stump; thick shape, bulb”), from Proto-Indo-European *gelt- (“something round, pregnant belly, child in the womb”), from *gel- (“to ball up, amass”). Cognate with Faroese koltur (“colt, foal”) Norwegian kult (“treestump”), Swedish kult (“young boar, piglet, boy, lad”) / Swedish kulting (“piglet”). Related to child.

ex.en: The wildest colt makes the best horse.
ex.ja: 最も野性的な子馬が最高の駿馬になる。

en: A public building housing courts of law.
The public building where most American counties have their county offices.

ex.en: Were you at the courthouse?
ex.ja: 裁判所にいたの？

ex.en: "You can get it at the courthouse," the clerk added.
ex.ja: 「都庁舎でもらえますよ」と係員が付け加えた。

ex.en: The woman left and went to the courthouse, where she waited in line again.
ex.ja: 都庁舎に行き、そこでまた列の中で待った。

en: Damn.
Damned.
Damn.
Damn.

ex.en: Darn it, I forgot my camera!
ex.ja: あ、カメラ忘れた！

ex.en: Although you can't compare them to Radiohead, Kashmir is a pretty darn good band.
ex.ja: ラジオヘッドとは比べるべくもないが、カシミールはなかないいバンドだよ。

en: To cause an intense dislike for something.
An intense dislike or loathing someone feels for something bad or nasty.

disgust.ety:
Borrowed from Middle French desgouster, from Old French desgouster (“to put off one's appetite”), from des- (“dis-”) + gouster, goster (“to taste”), from Latin gustus (“a tasting”). By surface analysis, dis- + gust (“taste”).
The noun is from Middle French desgoust, from the verb.

ex.en: When it comes to raw fish, I feel disgusted.
ex.ja: 生の魚となると気分が悪くなってしまうのです。

ex.en: I am disgusted with myself for my short memory.
ex.ja: 忘れっぽいのには自分ながら呆れる。

ex.en: I always view this photo with disgust.
ex.ja: この写真を見るとむかつく。

en: The termination of an organized body or legislative assembly, especially a formal dismissal.
Disintegration, or decomposition into fragments.

dissolution.ety: From Middle English dissolucioun, from Old French dissolucion, from Latin dissolūtiō (“a dissolving, destroying, breaking up, dissolution”).

ex.en: Justice without mercy is cruelty; mercy without justice is the mother of dissolution.
ex.ja: 哀れみのない正義は冷酷である。しかし、正義のない哀れみは解体の母である。

en: The act of disturbing, being disturbed.
Something that disturbs.

disturbance.ety: From Middle English disturbaunce, from Old French destorbance, destourbance, from destourber (“disturb”), from Latin disturbō. By surface analysis, disturb + -ance.

ex.en: The police intervened in the disturbance.
ex.ja: 警察が騒動に介入した。

en: Something that is enclosed, i.e. inserted into a letter or similar package.
The act of enclosing, i.e. the insertion or inclusion of an item in a letter or package.

enclosure.ety: From Middle English enclosure, from Old French enclosure, from enclore, from Latin inclūdere, inclūdō, from in- (“in”) + claudō (“to shut”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂u- (“key, hook, nail”). Alike to inclusion. By surface analysis, enclose + -ure.

ex.en: There are many kinds of animals inside this enclosure.
ex.ja: この囲いの中には何種類もの動物がいます。

en: Especially or extraordinarily fine or pleasing; exceptional.
Recherché; far-fetched; abstruse.

exquisite.ety: From Latin exquīsītus (“to be outsought”), perfect passive participle of exquīrō (“to outseek”).

ex.en: This is an exquisite little painting.
ex.ja: これは小さくて極めて美しい絵画だ。

ex.en: This soup is exquisite.
ex.ja: なんておいしいスープなんだろう。

ex.en: The tourists were fascinated with the exquisite scenery.
ex.ja: 観光客達はその素晴らしい風景にうっとりした。

en: Pertaining to or consisting of objective claims.
True, accurate, corresponding to reality.
Programmes having content based on facts, such as documentaries.

factual.ety: From fact + -ual, modeled after, and by analogy with, actual.

falsely.ety: From Middle English falsly, falsliche, equivalent to false + -ly.

ex.en: I was falsely accused.
ex.ja: 濡れ衣を着せられた。

en: Extreme shortage of food in a region.
A period of extreme shortage of food in a region.

famine.ety: Borrowed from Middle French famine, itself from the root of Latin fames.

ex.en: These countries were often visited with famine.
ex.ja: これらの国はしばしば飢饉に襲われた。

ex.en: War has produced famine throughout history.
ex.ja: 戦争は歴史上ずっと飢餓を引き起こしてきた。

ex.en: That is why so many people are suffering from famine.
ex.ja: それが、こんなに多数の人が饑饉で苦しんでいる理由です。

False, phony.

fraudulent.ety: From Middle English fraudulent, from Old French fraudulent, from Latin fraudulentus, from fraus (“fraud”).

ex.ja: 騙りメールにご注意ください。

ex.ja: くれぐれも浄水器の悪質訪問販売業者や無料点検商法にはご注意ください。

en: A highway with grade-separated crossings (rather than level crossings) and designed (and only permitted) for high-speed motor-traffic run…
A toll-free highway.

ex.ja: 高速道路で悲惨な事故があった。

ex.en: He came by the freeway.
ex.ja: 彼は高速道路を通ってやってきた。

ex.en: There are roads and freeways wherever you go in America.
ex.ja: アメリカでは、どこへ行っても立派な道路と高速道路がある。

en: Recently, newly.
In a rude or impertinent manner.

freshly.ety: From Middle English freschely, freschliche (also as ferscheli, fersly, ferselich), equivalent to fresh + -ly.

ex.en: They sell us freshly caught fish in the early morning market.
ex.ja: 彼らは捕り立ての魚を朝市で売ってくれる。

ex.en: The fish is freshly caught.
ex.ja: とれたての魚です。

ex.en: I like the smell of freshly-baked bread.
ex.ja: 焼きたてのパンの匂いが好きです。

An official periodical publication published by a government containing legal and state notices, and in some cases, legislations, subsidi…
To publish (something) in a gazette.
To announce the status of (someone) in an official gazette; this pertained to both appointments and bankruptcies.

gazette.ety: Borrowed from French gazette, from Italian gazzetta, from Venetan gazeta, from gazeta dele novità (literally “a gazeta (halfpenny) of news”), named for the cost (one gazeta) of the newspaper. Compare penny dreadful, dime novel. See gazzetta for more.

en: A person who is intensely interested in a particular field or hobby and often having limited or nonstandard social skills. Often used wit…
An expert in a technical field, particularly one having to do with computers.
To perform bizarre and unpleasant feats as part of a carnival.
To enthusiastically engage in geek-like or nerdy interests.

geek.ety: Started as carnival slang, likely from the British dialectal term geck (“a fool, dupe, simpleton”) (1510s), apparently from Dutch gek or Low German geck, from an imitative verb found in North Sea Germanic and Scandinavian meaning "to croak, cackle," and also "to mock, cheat" (Dutch gekken, German gecken, Danish gække, Norwegian gakke, Swedish gäcka). The root still survives in the Dutch adjective noun gek (“crazy" or "crazy person”). Compare gink and also Old Norse gikkr (“a pert, rude person; jester; fool”).

ex.en: Tom is a math geek.
ex.ja: トムは数学オタクです。

ex.en: Tom is a language geek.
ex.ja: トムは言語オタクだ。

Any elderly woman, regardless of if she has grandchildren.

ex.ja: うちのおばあちゃん、漬物名人なのよ。

An allowance of a certain amount of time or distance in starting, granted in a race (or other contest of skill) to the competitor possess…

To place at disadvantage.

ex.en: You can get over the handicap soon.
ex.ja: すぐにその困難は乗り越えられるよ。

ex.en: The blind young man has got over his handicap.
ex.ja: 目の不自由なその青年はハンディキャップを克服した。

A hostile action, especially a military action. See hostilities for specific plural definition.

hostility.ety: From Middle English hostilitie, hostilite, from Old French hostilité, from Latin hostīlitās. By surface analysis, hostile + -ity.

ex.en: I have no personal hostility to the system.
ex.ja: その制度に対する個人的な敵意はない。

ex.en: Hostility was replaced by love.
ex.ja: 敵意に代わって愛情が生まれた。

en: A song of praise or worship, especially a religious one.
To sing a hymn.
To praise or extol in hymns.

hymn.ety: From Middle English ymne, from Old English ymen (reinforced by Old French ymne), from Latin hymnus, borrowed from Ancient Greek ὕμνος (húmnos).

ex.en: The morning service began with a hymn.
ex.ja: 朝の礼拝は賛美歌ではじまった。

Conditional; contingent upon some hypothesis/antecedent.
A possible or hypothetical situation or proposition.
A violation or breach, as of a law.
An encroachment on a right, a person, a territory, or a property.

The first year of a medical residency.

Stimulating or exciting a response.

The perfume obtained from these plants.

The deactivation of anything.
Rendering someone unconscious.
Amazing; gorgeous; beautiful.

ex.en: He won the fight by a knockout.
ex.ja: 彼はノックアウト勝ちした。

en: A case of translucent or transparent material made to protect a flame, or light, used to illuminate its surroundings.
Especially, a metal casing with lens used to illuminate a stage (e.g. spotlight, floodlight).
To furnish with a lantern.
Of a facial feature, large and squarish in shape as an old-fashioned lantern.

lantern.ety: From Middle English lanterne (13th century), via Old French lanterne from Latin lanterna (“lantern”), itself a corruption of Ancient Greek λαμπτήρ (lamptḗr, “torch”) (see lamp, λάμπω (lámpō)) by influence of Latin lucerna (“lamp”). The spelling lanthorn was current during the 16th to 19th centuries and originates with a folk etymology associating the word with the use of horn as translucent cover. For the verb, compare French lanterner to hang at the lamppost. Displaced native Old English lēohtfæt (literally “light-container”).

ex.en: Tom held up the lantern.
ex.ja: トムはランタンを掲げた。

ex.en: The forest was illuminate​d by a lantern.
ex.ja: ランタンが林を照らした。

ex.ja: 九頭竜明神を祭るために灯篭をながす。

Made from linen cloth or thread.
Having the colour linen, light beige.

linen.ety: From Middle English lynnen, lynen, from Old English līnen (“linen", "made of flax”), from Proto-West Germanic *līnīn (“made of flax”), from Proto-Germanic *līną (“flax”), from Proto-Indo-European *līno- (“flax”), equivalent to line + -en. Cognate with Latin līnum (“flax”) and thus also Linum. More at line.

ex.ja: うちの恥をさらすな。

To make a night-time attack on a tenant farmer not supporting the policies of the Irish National Land League.
